items.abstract: <jats:p>AbstractHydrogen-based sector coupling is increasingly proposed as a pathway for deep decarbonization because it connects variable renewable electricity with hard-to-electrify industrial, mobility, heat and long-duration balancing demands. This study develops a transparent techno-economic and environmental assessment framework for an integrated electricity-hydrogen energy system. The model co-optimizes renewable electricity use, grid interaction, electrolyze operation, hydrogen storage and sectoral allocation under representative hourly simulation inputs. Five scenarios are evaluated: fossil reference, grid electrolysis, renewable electrolysis, storage-enabled hydrogen production and fully integrated sector coupling. Results indicate that flexible electrolysis can absorb renewable surplus, reduce curtailment and lower emissions when operation is constrained by carbon intensity and supported by storage. The integrated configuration reduces system emissions and improves supply reliability relative to isolated hydrogen production, while levelized hydrogen cost remains most sensitive to electricity price, electrolyze capital cost, utilization and storage cost. Sectoral results show that industrial feedstock substitution and heavy mobility provide higher abatement value than routine low-temperature heat use under the assumed conditions. The study contributes a submission-ready applied energy systems framework that links physical dispatch, economic feasibility and environmental performance. Policy implications emphasize granular carbon certification, flexible electricity tariffs, hydrogen hub planning around anchor demand and prioritization of high-value end uses.</jats:p>
title: Hydrogen-Based Sector Coupling for Deep Decarbonization: Techno-Economic and Environmental Assessment of Integrated Energy Systems
